blocks.html:
The operators a search filter can apply to a field.

Filters are a tree rather than a string, because no two engines agree on a
filter syntax — Meilisearch, Typesense and Algolia each have their own DSL;
engines that take JSON filters compile from the same tree. A tree compiles to
all of them.

`$prefix` and `$like` are not universal — Meilisearch has no substring filter
at all — so a provider without them rejects them.

types.description:
The operators a search filter can apply to a field.

Filters are a tree rather than a string, because no two engines agree on a
filter syntax — Meilisearch, Typesense and Algolia each have their own DSL;
engines that take JSON filters compile from the same tree. A tree compiles to
all of them.

`$prefix` and `$like` are not universal — Meilisearch has no substring filter

children.name: $eq
children.description: The field must equal this value.

children.name: $ne
children.description: The field must not equal this value.

children.name: $in
children.description: The field must equal one of these values.

children.name: $nin
children.description: The field must not equal any of these values.

children.name: $lt
children.description: The field must be less than this value.

children.name: $lte
children.description: The field must be less than or equal to this value.

children.name: $gt
children.description: The field must be greater than this value.

children.name: $gte
children.description: The field must be greater than or equal to this value.

children.name: $exists
children.description: Whether the field must be set on the document.

children.name: $contains
children.description: The array field must contain all of the given values.

children.name: $overlaps
children.description: The array field must contain at least one of the given values.

children.name: $prefix
children.description: The field must start with this string.

children.name: $like
children.description: The field must contain this substring.
